turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so we have twenty minutes. Who decided Owen gets a zero, and why did he find out from his phone in the middle of class?
An answer to what, Hale? I'm the one asking the questions today. Nobody called me before that zero went in, and procedure 4.2 says somebody should have.
Either Owen admits it in writing by Friday at 3 PM or the zero goes on his transcript.

I'm writing that down: "Either Owen admits it in writing by Friday at 3 PM or the zero goes on his transcript." Owen will not be signing any confession, and you've shown me nothing but a machine's guess so far. Put that ultimatum in an email to me today, cc the principal, because that's where I'm going when I leave this room.
Those are the only two options. Pick one.

I'm not picking either one, Hale. Your own procedure says software alone doesn't establish a concern, and it gives me the right to ask the principal to review this, which I'm doing today. The zero comes off, and if you have anything a person can actually check, put it on the table now.
